# Vendored ROCm headers

These headers are vendored **only for compilation** of the HIP/Verbs Acceptance
Suite. No ROCm libraries are linked at build time; all HIP/HSA entry points are
resolved dynamically at run time through the `dlopen`/`dlsym` wrapper. The
headers therefore provide declarations and types only.

## Minimal (pruned) set

The login-node build uses plain g++ with no HIP toolchain, so these headers are
needed for **declarations only**. That host compile pulls in only the transitive
`#include` closure of the wrapper entry point `hip/utils/HipApi.hpp` — a couple
of dozen headers, not the full upstream tree. The device-side headers
(fp16/bf16/cooperative-groups/texture device functions/...) are used solely by
`hipcc` when regenerating the prebuilt kernel object (`build_static_kernels.sh`)
against a real `/opt/rocm`, never by this vendored set. This folder is therefore
**pruned to exactly that closure**; `update.sh` recomputes the closure on every
re-vendor, so the set self-adjusts if a future release reorganizes includes.

## Source

Vendored from the upstream ROCm monorepo, **not** from a local `/opt/rocm`
install:

- Repository: https://github.com/ROCm/rocm-systems
- Branch: `develop`
- Commit: `37723244ca8cd75d5e55d30f44c77af1bd49218b`

## Layout / provenance

| Vendored path        | Upstream path                                                    |
| -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `hip/*.h`            | `projects/hip/include/hip/`                                      |
| `hip/amd_detail/`    | `projects/clr/hipamd/include/hip/amd_detail/`                    |
| `hsa/`               | `projects/rocr-runtime/runtime/hsa-runtime/inc/`                |

The public HIP headers live in the `hip` project while the AMD backend detail
headers live in the `clr` (hipamd) project; ROCm merges them into a single
`hip/` include tree at install time, which is reproduced here (then pruned).

`hip/hip_version.h` is normally generated by the CLR build system and is not
present in the source tree; `update.sh` writes a fixed copy (see that file).

## Updating to a new ROCm version (e.g. 7.15)

Use the script — it sparse-checks out the three upstream directories at the
requested ref, generates `hip_version.h`, prunes to the exact header closure,
refreshes the **Source** provenance below, and verifies the wrappers still
compile:

```sh
# run from the project root (hip-verbs-acceptance/)
vendor/rocm-headers/update.sh release/rocm-rel-7.15
```

Pick a release tag/branch (reproducible) over `develop`. If the ref name does not
carry the version, pass it explicitly:

```sh
HIP_VERSION_MAJOR=7 HIP_VERSION_MINOR=15 HIP_VERSION_PATCH=0 \
  vendor/rocm-headers/update.sh <ref>
```

Then rebuild and run the gate before committing:

```sh
cmake -S . -B build -DACCEPT_WITH_HIP=ON && cmake --build build -j
git status vendor/rocm-headers     # review added/removed headers
```

Notes:

- The script keeps only the `g++ -M` closure of `hip/utils/HipApi.hpp`. If a new
  release reorganizes includes, the closure (and thus the vendored set) adjusts
  automatically — no manual file list to maintain.
- If a newly added API changed signature or an ABI alias name changed, the
  verify step (or the real build) will flag it; adjust the ops-table / redirect
  block in `hip/wrapper/*` accordingly. Symbols that exist in the headers but not
  in the installed runtime are fine — `init()` reports them as missing and the
  dependent tests skip (see `checked_op` / `MissingSymbol`).
- `KEEP_FULL=1 vendor/rocm-headers/update.sh <ref>` vendors the full upstream
  copy instead of pruning (debugging only).
